facts.text: On this date in 1939, Germany invaded Poland — but France and Britain, despite declaring war two days later, launched no real offensive for eight months. The 'Phoney War' left Poland to fall alone.
On this date in 1715, Louis XIV died after ruling France for 72 years — longer than any other major European monarch in history. He outlived his son, grandson, and great-grandson heir.
Manila is the most densely populated city on Earth, packing over 111,000 people per square kilometer — denser than any borough of New York, any district of Tokyo, anywhere.
Canada has more lakes than every other country on Earth combined, holding roughly 60% of the world's fresh surface lake water within its borders.

Indonesia is home to more volcanoes than any country on Earth — around 130 active ones — and sits atop so much geothermal energy that it remains largely untapped despite chronic electricity shortages.
On this day in 1998, Russia defaulted on its domestic debt, triggering a global financial panic that destroyed Long-Term Capital Management — a hedge fund run by two Nobel laureates.
On September 1, 1939, the same day Germany invaded Poland, the New York Stock Exchange opened normally and closed up on the day.
The Dutch East India Company paid an uninterrupted dividend for 200 years, making it history's most durable income investment — it also had its own army, navy, and the power to wage war.
Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway originally made textiles. He later called buying it the worst trade of his life, estimating the mistake cost him $200 billion in compounded opportunity.
The entire U.S. bond market is roughly twice the size of the U.S. stock market — most of the money in finance moves through an asset class most people never think about.
On this date in 1859, the Carrington Event began — the most powerful solar storm ever recorded. It made auroras visible in Cuba and set telegraph wires on fire without any power source connected.

On this date in 1979, Pioneer 11 became the first spacecraft to fly past Saturn, revealing that its rings are almost entirely empty space — more vacuum than the best vacuum humans can create on Earth.
Your bones are not passive scaffolding. They secrete a hormone called osteocalcin that regulates memory, fertility, and your body's response to sudden danger — effectively acting as a gland.
A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere roughly the size of a city. A single teaspoon of its material would weigh about a billion tons on Earth.

Tardigrades can survive the vacuum of open space, absorbed doses of radiation that would kill a human 1,000 times over, and temperatures near absolute zero — all without any special adaptation beyond cryptobiosis.
On this day in 1939, Germany invaded Poland — but France and Britain's declaration of war came two days later. Hitler genuinely believed they were bluffing, again.
Oxford University was already 300 years old when the Aztec Empire was founded. We casually call both 'ancient civilizations.'
On this day in 1985, the wreck of the Titanic was located. It had been on the ocean floor longer by then than it had been a working ship.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid. Egypt's own history dwarfs our imagination of it.
The fax machine was patented in 1843 — before the American Civil War, before the telephone, before the light bulb. Your office's most hated device is older than modernity.

Sonder (n.): the realization that each passerby has a life as vivid and complex as your own. Coined by John Koenig in The Dictionary of Obscure Sorrows, 2012 — invented, yet it filled a gap language had no business leaving empty.

Hiraeth (n.): a Welsh longing for a home that may never have existed. It folds homesickness, grief, and nostalgia into one word that English, despite borrowing from everywhere, never managed to build.

On this day in 1939, Germany invaded Poland — and the word 'blitzkrieg' entered global vocabulary within weeks. Meaning 'lightning war' in German, it was largely a term coined by foreign journalists, not the Wehrmacht itself.

Mamihlapinatapai: a Yaghan word from Tierra del Fuego describing a look shared between two people who both want something but neither will initiate. The language has one living native speaker as of the 2020s.

On September 1, 1878, Emma Nutt became the world's first female telephone operator in Boston. The word 'operator' descends from Latin 'operari' — to work, to take effect — and quietly outlasted every technology it once named.
On this date in 2017, Bitcoin's SegWit upgrade activated after a years-long civil war. It separated signature data from transaction data, doubling effective block capacity without a hard fork.
On this date in 2021, Ethereum's EIP-1559 had been live for 26 days, having already burned over 100,000 ETH — permanently removing it from supply via ordinary transaction fees.

Satoshi's genesis block coinbase contains the text 'The Times 03/Jan/2009 Chancellor on brink of second bailout for banks' — both a timestamp and an editorial statement baked immutably into Bitcoin's first block.
The DAO hack of 2016 drained 3.6 million ETH through a reentrancy bug. The attacker couldn't move the funds immediately — a 28-day lock gave Ethereum enough time to hard-fork and reverse the theft.

Bitcoin's difficulty adjustment recalculates every 2,016 blocks, targeting a 10-minute average. It has no external oracle — the network self-corrects purely through elapsed timestamps recorded by miners.

On this date in 2009, Kickstarter launched — the same year Hinton's group at Toronto was quietly scaling deep belief nets that would, three years later, halve ImageNet error rates and reboot the entire field.
On this date in 2017, Google Brain published the Transformer paper. 'Attention Is All You Need' was rejected from one workshop before acceptance; it now has over 100,000 citations.
AlphaFold 2 predicted structures for roughly 200 million proteins — nearly every catalogued protein known to science — in a run that would have taken conventional crystallography thousands of years.

GPT-4 was trained on roughly 25,000 A100-equivalents for an estimated $100M in compute. The entire compute budget of the Manhattan Project, inflation-adjusted, was about $2.2B — the gap is closing fast.
The first neural network to beat a human champion at Go, AlphaGo, was itself defeated nine months later by AlphaGo Zero, which learned entirely from self-play with no human game data whatsoever.
